ietf-rfc1918.name: RFC 1918 (Address Allocation for Private Internets) and related reserved-range RFCs (3927, 5735/6890)
ietf-rfc1918.note: Long-stable, widely-known internet standard reference - written from general technical knowledge of these RFCs' contents rather than a fresh fetch, since the private/reserved IP ranges they define have not changed in decades.

iana-port-registry.name: Service Name and Transport Protocol Port Number Registry
iana-port-registry.note: The authoritative registry for port number assignments; this page cites only the small set of long-stable, extremely well-known ports (HTTP/HTTPS/SSH/DNS/DHCP/etc.), not an attempt to reproduce the full registry.

general-networking-education.name: General computer networking/computing technical education
general-networking-education.note: Widely-taught networking/computing concepts (Wi-Fi terminology, Ethernet/cabling, USB/serial, checksums/hashes, text encoding) not tied to one specific regulatory citation - the same pattern already used elsewhere in this project (e.g. Maps' general-nav-education, Radio's general-rf-education).

ietf-rfc20-ascii.name: RFC 20 (ASCII format for Network Interchange)
ietf-rfc20-ascii.publisher: IETF (Internet Engineering Task Force) / Vint Cerf, 1969
ietf-rfc20-ascii.note: The original IETF standard defining ASCII for network interchange - directly grounds this page's ASCII coverage. Citation-only (same pattern as ietf-rfc1918/iana-port-registry below) - a 128-character 7-bit table has not changed since 1969, nothing to re-fetch. Does not itself cover Unicode/UTF-8 (which postdates it by decades) - general-networking-education remains the secondary source for that half of the entry.

neets13-number-systems-logic.name: Introduction to Number Systems and Logic (NEETS Module 13)
neets13-number-systems-logic.note: Already retained in the Document Library (not computing-specific, but the only retained source touching how binary/digital signaling represents data) - grounds usb-serial-basics' underlying digital-logic concept, not USB or RS-232 specifically. No dedicated public-domain USB/RS-232 standard was found this round (USB-IF's own specification and TIA-232-F are both proprietary/licensed, not freely redistributable) - see docs/IMPLEMENTATION-ROADMAP.md round 8 for what was checked and rejected.
